topic: Thread Unjoinability Issue: Absence of Standard `std::thread` RAII Wrapper
explanation: Assumption: All resource-owning types in the Standard Library have corresponding RAII wrappers to ensure cleanup (via destruction) regardless of the control flow path (exceptions, returns, jumps). Reality: The Standard Library notably lacks a standard RAII wrapper for `std::thread` objects. Why It Fails: The standardization committee could not agree on a default behavior for a thread object going out of scope—should it automatically `join()` (wait for termination) or `detach()` (run in the background)? This lack of consensus means developers must manually implement RAII wrappers (like a `thread_guard` class) to ensure that every `std::thread` is either joined or detached before its destructor runs, preventing program termination via `std::terminate` when an unjoined, non-detached thread goes out of scope.
practical_example: A function launches a background thread to calculate a result, but an exception is thrown before the `t.join()` call is reached. Since there is no RAII guard, the thread object is destroyed while still joinable, triggering immediate program termination and losing the application state.
chapter: Item 37: Ensure std::threads are joinable on all paths
